name: table-pull
desc: Free, open-source table extractor for Windows — PDFs and scans to CSV or Excel with a grid fixer. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Tables from scans** — bordered or borderless tables in scanned PDFs detected and pulled into rows
✅ **Grid fixer** — adjust columns and merge split cells visually before export, not in a text editor
✅ **CSV and XLSX out** — one click to a spreadsheet, with number formatting preserved where confidence allows
✅ **Multi-page stitching** — a table spanning twelve pages comes out as one continuous sheet
✅ **Batch documents** — fifty financial reports processed into fifty CSV files on a schedule
✅ **Confidence shading** — uncertain cells tinted so review goes where it matters
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime and OCR engine bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Price | **Free, MIT** | Free, OSS | Free, OSS | Subscription |
| Scanned PDF support | **Yes** | No | No | Partial
| Visual grid fixer | **Yes** | No | No | Partial
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Java env | Python env | Installer
faqQ: extract tables from scanned PDFs into Excel on Windows for free?
faqA: Classic open tools only read digital text layers, so scans come out as garbage, and commercial suites lock export behind a subscription. table-pull detects tables in scans, lets you fix the grid visually and exports CSV or XLSX. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline, batch included.
s1: Dark extractor (#121417, slate #64748B): scanned report page left with a detected table outlined, extracted grid right with confidence shading, export CSV button lit.
s2: Grid fixer: one split cell highlighted, merge button armed, column drag handle mid-move, undo row beneath with step list.
s3: Batch results: 50 report files each mapped to a CSV with row counts, one amber file flagged for review, folder summary chip reading 12,408 rows total.
